snippet.description:
Freddy & Juan Discover The Gold That Could Save Morgan’s Mine

Morgan is more than fifty ounces — over a hundred and seventy-five thousand dollars — behind his season target, with a dying cut beneath him and barely a month before the freeze shuts everything down. His mine is quietly leaking gold he can't even see, and the ground that carried his whole season is almost gone. So Freddy Dodge and Juan Ibarra start hunting across his claim for the one thing that could turn it all around: white channel, the pale ancient gravel that built the Klondike. Find enough of it, and Morgan keeps his mine. Come up empty, and the easy years are over.

snippet.title: New Discoveries Rewrite Maya History | Rise and Fall of the Maya MEGA Episode | National Geographic
snippet.description:
What actually happened to the ancient Maya? Mysteries unfold in this four episode Rise and Fall of the Maya Mega Episode compilation from National Geographic. Journey where the Maya lived in Mexico and Guatemala as archaeologists and historians uncover new evidence that rewrites what we know about this fascinating and mysterious ancient civilization. From the monumental discovery of a 3,000-year-old hidden megastructure to the puzzling, catastrophic collapse that forced millions to abandon their pyramid-filled cities, explore the origins of Maya power, secrets, and resilience in this documentary series. Featuring full episodes: 

Origins - 00:00 
What is Aguada Fénix? In June 2020, scientists discover Aguada Fénix, a monumental 3,000-year-old Maya structure. Uncover the hidden secrets of Aguada Fénix, the oldest monument built by the ancient Maya civilization, dating back to around 1000 BCE, that challenge everything we knew about the Maya's earliest days.

Civilization - 44:03 
New architectural and technological evidence unearthed in Mexico’s Yucatán Peninsula transforms long-held ideas about how the Maya civilization grew into a superpower.

Collapse - 01:28:06
Why did the ancient Maya civilization collapse? Many cities were abandoned due to a complex combination of severe droughts, overpopulation, deforestation, and warfare. The exact series of events that lead the ancient Maya to abandon their pyramid-filled cities has long puzzled archaeologists. Now, new investigations in Mexico and Guatemala are exposing surprising evidence about why these great monuments were deserted. 

Resilience - 02:12:09
Archaeologists unearth new clues about the resurgence of the ancient Maya civilization and the devastating events that would ultimately lead them to abandon their cities for good. Investigations also reveal evidence of extreme resilience in the face of catastrophe.

snippet.title: Alabama’s Hidden Millions: Pirate Gold, Lost Payroll & Spanish Shipwrecks
snippet.description:
Alabama is known for cotton fields, college football, and Gulf Coast beaches… but for more than 300 years this state has quietly swallowed pirate treasure, Civil War gold payrolls, Spanish shipwreck fortunes, and millions in modern beach jewelry that is still being found today.

In this episode of Campfire Creepers – Travels Stranger Than Fiction, we count down the Top 3 Hidden Treasures of Alabama plus one bonus treasure you could realistically find on your very next trip to the Gulf Coast.

From the pirate activity near Bon Secour River and Fort Morgan, to the lost Union gold payroll along the Alabama River near Selma, to the overlooked Spanish wreck zone of Mobile Bay, Dauphin Island, and Fort Gaines, Alabama may be one of the richest overlooked treasure landscapes in America.

And unlike many legends, some of this treasure is still being found after storms along the beaches of Gulf Shores, Orange Beach, Gulf State Park, Dauphin Island, and Fort Morgan.

This is also why many treasure hunters quietly prefer Alabama over crowded Florida hotspots like Destin, Panama City, Clearwater, or the Florida Keys — the beaches are less commercial, less crowded, more affordable for families, and the sand movement after storms regularly reveals jewelry, coins, and historic artifacts.

If you enjoy metal detecting, beach combing, history, travel adventure, or treasure hunting, Alabama’s Gulf Coast might be your next great road trip.

snippet.title: 1776: The Uncensored Story of The American Revolution
snippet.description:
Forget what you learned in school. Or from Hamilton. The American revolution was bigger and bloodier than you ever thought.

For the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence, we bring you the undiscovered stories, heroes, and villains of the War for Independence. In this incredible six-part retelling, we go far beyond the 13 original colonies and the clash between American Patriots and British colonial troops. We traverse the Atlantic and plunge deep into the American West to discover a multi-front war that engulfed a diverse cast of characters – Indigenous people, enslaved Africans, American Loyalists, women of all social classes – and changed the face of world history.

EPISODE 1: UNLIKELY REVOLUTIONARIES 
We begin by profiling three unlikely revolutionaries: George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, and John Adams. 

EPISODE 2: REVOLUTION IN INDIAN COUNTRY 
When fighting breaks out between Britain and the American colonists, the native people of North America are forced to pick a side. 

EPISODE 3: THE SLAVES’ REVOLUTION
The American War for Independence was, in fact, two revolutions in one. There was the Revolution we know – of American Patriots against their British overlords. And there was the Revolution we don’t know – of enslaved Black people against their American overlords
